instruction: I don't want to see the user switch option when my screen is locked. Can you disable the user switching feature on the lock screen?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires disabling user switching on the lock screen. Config sets user-switch-enabled to true, instruction asks to disable it. The evaluator checks if the setting is false. Uses existing exact_match metric with vm_command_line getter.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement to disable user switching on lock screen
Getter appropriately reads the gsettings value for org.gnome.desktop.screensaver user-switch-enabled
Metric exact_match is suitable for checking boolean setting values
Expected value 'false\n' is correct - matches gsettings output format with newline
Complete coverage: instruction asks to disable, evaluator checks if setting is false
No state timing issues or edge cases - gsettings command is reliable and immediate
